chapter: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
title: Eddie Heywood at Cafe Society and a short spell with Benny Carter
summary: His first real solo chance came with Eddie Heywood at Cafe Society, recording with Billie Holiday; Benny Carter's Savoy band soon folded.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: The only time that I really got a

good first opportunity is when I joined Eddie Heywood at the Cafe Society. Then, he gave me -- I was the only trumpet player and what little solos were to be played on trumpet, I did it. But not too much, but most of his music was ensemble.
That's sort of like being pushed into the pool and learning how to swim?
That's right. And I was with Eddie, recorded with Billie Holiday at that time.
But were also with Bennie Carter -- briefly
Oh, yes. Very short time because he wasn't making any money at the Savoy.
Yes. He gave up and he went on to California.
I see. But, we're back to 1939 and 1940, did you do a lot of Cafe Society gigs?
